question: A 41-year-old female complains of frequent diarrhea and abdominal pain between meals. Endoscopy reveals a duodenal ulcer distal to the duodenal bulb. CT scan of the abdomen demonstrates a pancreatic mass, and subsequent tissue biopsy of the pancreas reveals a malignant islet cell tumor. Which of the following hormones is likely to be markedly elevated in this patient:?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Malignant islet cell tumor in the pancreas" -> "Excessive production of hormones by the tumor" -> "Markedly elevated levels of hormones" -> 95% CHAIN: "Malignant islet cell tumor in the pancreas" -> "Excessive production of gastrin" -> "Markedly elevated gastrin levels" -> 95%
enhanced_information: A malignant islet cell tumor in the pancreas can lead to excessive production of hormones, with markedly elevated levels of gastrin being a common outcome. Evidence paths support the association of pancreatic tumors with hormone production, specifically gastrins, aligning with the likelihood of markedly elevated gastrin levels in this patient.
analysis: The core medical principle here is the association of a malignant islet cell tumor in the pancreas with excessive hormone production. In this context, markedly elevated levels of gastrin are commonly seen. Gastrinoma, a type of islet cell tumor, can lead to Zollinger-Ellison syndrome characterized by increased gastrin secretion. This aligns with the enhanced information provided, indicating that gastrin is likely to be markedly elevated in this patient.
